gaps: query_metric calls for pool wait p95, pool timeout rate, DB operation p95 and request rate were cut off with budget_exhausted (ev_10, ev_11, ev_12), so the trigger that first pinned the event loop is unconfirmed.
log_patterns over the incident window returned budget_exhausted (ev_13, ev_15), so warn-level log patterns naming a blocking call were not examined.
search_logs for error/exception details returned budget_exhausted (ev_14); only aggregate log volume by severity (ev_1) is available.
Node/process CPU and memory metrics were not queried at all, so CPU limits vs. busy-loop vs. memory pressure within the event-loop saturation could not be separated.
No deployment, config-change or traffic-routing events were checked for the period preceding 19:22:19Z.

Whether pool saturation is upstream of the event loop was not settled: a pool_timeout_rate above zero or a DB latency spike would have contradicted the event-loop-first ordering but neither was retrieved.
report.summary: Latency p95 on demo-service rose from a millisecond-scale baseline to multi-second values starting 19:22:19Z, with no 5xx errors and no error logs. Event-loop utilization pinning at 1.0 is the first resource signal to move and precedes pool saturation and request queueing by one sample, so event-loop saturation most probably starved pool turnover; pool exhaustion is downstream. Metrics for pool wait, DB latency and request rate could not be read before the budget ran out, so the trigger is unconfirmed.

timeline.event: Baseline: latency_p95 at {lat_first} s and eventloop_utilization near 0.07, pool_pending 0.
eventloop_utilization jumps to {el_at_onset}; latency_p95 rises to 0.4389503347498711 s; pool_used climbs to 7 connections.
Event loop reaches 1.0 utilization, pool_used hits {pool_used_last} connections (pool_max {pool_max}) and pool_pending reaches {pend_max}; latency_p95 at 1.8958288760971762 s.
latency_p95 peaks at {lat_max} s and the http-latency-p95 rule fires; error_ratio_5xx remains {err_max}.

hypotheses.statement: Event-loop saturation in demo-service pinned eventloop_utilization at {el_max} from 19:22:34 onward, stalling request handling so that p95 latency rose to {lat_max} s while no errors were produced.
Exhaustion of the fixed-size connection pool (pool_used reaching pool_max of {pool_max} connections with {pend_max} pending requests) caused the latency spike to {lat_max} s.
A surge in downstream/database response time starved the event loop and filled the pool, driving p95 latency to {lat_max} s with queued work of {pend_max} pending requests.

observations.statement: latency_p95 was flat near 9 ms through the pre-incident baseline window, with a maximum of {lat_base} s.

In the incident window latency_p95 rose from a first sample of {lat_first} s to a maximum of {lat_max} s at 19:22:49.571Z, with intermediate samples of 0.4389503347498711 s at 19:22:19 and 1.8958288760971762 s at 19:22:34.
eventloop_utilization rose abruptly from ~0.06 to {el_at_onset} at the 19:22:19.571Z sample and then saturated at {el_max} (ratio 1.0) from 19:22:34.571Z onward, with max_at 19:22:34.571Z.
Before 19:22:19 eventloop_utilization stayed between {el_min} and about 0.07, i.e. far from saturation.
pool_used was 0-1 connections until 19:22:04.571Z and then reached {pool_used_last} connections at 19:22:34.571Z, against a fixed pool_max of {pool_max} connections.
pool_pending was 0 for the whole baseline window (max {pend_base}) but reached {pend_max} waiting requests in the incident window at 19:22:34.571Z.
error_ratio_5xx stayed exactly at {err_max} for all 10 samples of the incident window.

Log volume in the incident window shows only info and warn severities: warn ranged {warn_min} to {warn_max} lines per minute (sum 33) while info ranged {info_min} to {info_max} lines per minute, with no error severity present.

recommendations.action: Profile the demo-service event loop during the 19:22:19-19:22:49Z window to identify the synchronous/CPU-heavy code path that pinned utilization at 1.0 (long stack traces, blocking calls, or large synchronous JSON/CPU work).
recommendations.rationale: hyp_1 attributes the incident to event-loop saturation that began one sample before pool saturation; naming the blocking call is required to fix the root cause.

recommendations.action: Add event-loop lag/utilization alerting with an earlier threshold than the p95 rule so saturation is paged before latency breaches the SLO.
recommendations.rationale: eventloop_utilization moved to {el_at_onset} at 19:22:19, roughly 30 s before detection at 19:22:49.

recommendations.action: Instrument and alert on pool wait time and pool pending depth, and evaluate whether pool_max of {pool_max} connections is adequate for demo-service.
recommendations.rationale: hyp_2 cannot be fully excluded because pool_wait_p95 and pool_timeout_rate were never read; pool depth and pending counts would distinguish a genuine pool bottleneck from a downstream effect.

recommendations.action: Query db_operation_p95 and request_rate for the 19:20-19:23Z window to determine whether a slow query or a traffic surge initiated the stall.
recommendations.rationale: hyp_3 (dependency latency or traffic-driven stall) is untested since those metrics were not retrieved before the budget ran out.
